summary:
Ağrı stands under the national legal framework of Türkiye; the source inventory records no province-specific statute, ordinance, enforcement pattern or incident series applying to the province. What a trans visitor encounters in Ağrı is Turkish national law and national police practice as described in the parent record.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's omnibus 11th Judicial Package would open the way to criminal charges against LGBT people, described there as one of the most alarming rollbacks of rights in decades. Conduct deemed 'contrary to biological sex and general morality', including its so-called 'promotion', would carry up to three years in prison, and participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies up to four years; same-sex marriage is not legal in Türkiye, so such ceremonies are by definition symbolic. The package would also restrict gender-affirming care: raising the surgery age from 18 to 25, making permanent infertility mandatory, exposing medical professionals to fines or up to seven years' imprisonment, and imprisoning transgender patients for up to three years for care outside the new limits, which would push treatment into underground settings. The package contains no Ağrı-specific provision, and whether it has since been enacted is unresolved in the sources.

Kaos GL's report on 2025, 'A Major Siege against LGBTI+ People in 2025: Hostility Turned into State Policy', documents six right-to-life violations, three recorded as hate-motivated killings, with trans people the most affected. These counts are drawn from media and civil-society reports because the state keeps no official hate-crime statistics. The report also records 89 torture or ill-treatment violations, up from 51 the previous year, mostly linked to peaceful assembly, alongside 336 assembly violations and 313 liberty violations — a roughly 2.5-fold rise in liberty violations, consisting mostly of detentions — together with event-specific bans and violent police attacks on peaceful gatherings. Hostility is presented as institutionalised under 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions, with hate speech from senior officials, censored broadcasts and cancelled artistic events. The report describes national practice rather than provincial choice, and no Ağrı-specific finding appears in it.
tangentialFactors:
The 2025 hostility documented by Kaos GL is described as national policy rather than a matter of local discretion, so a trans visitor in Ağrı should expect the same framework of detentions, assembly restrictions and official rhetoric recorded elsewhere in Türkiye, even though no Ağrı-specific incident appears in the inventory.

The draft 11th Judicial Package reported by Human Rights Watch would, if enacted, reshape exposure nationwide, including in Ağrı: criminal liability for LGBT 'promotion', ceremony participation, and gender-affirming care obtained outside new limits. Whether the package has passed remains unresolved in the sources.
localsOnly: Trans residents of Ağrı, like trans people across Türkiye, would face the national framework described in the parent record: detention patterns documented at scale in 2025, restrictions on gender-affirming care under the draft judicial package, and hostility institutionalised through 'Year of the Family' instructions to public institutions. The inventory records no Ağrı-specific enforcement data, local ordinance or provincial practice.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since Human Rights Watch's 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

The inventory contains no Ağrı-specific data on policing, detentions, healthcare access for trans residents, or local civil-society presence; the province-level picture rests entirely on the national framework carried by the parent record.

Kaos GL's counts derive from media and civil-society monitoring because Türkiye maintains no official hate-crime statistics, so the true scale of violations in any province, Ağrı included, is not sourced.
